title: Stack provenance report
description: What a selection's sources say their pixel values are, before anything is stacked. Emitted identically by `umbra stack --provenance --json` (umbra_py.StackProvenance.to_dict), `POST /artifacts/provenance` on `umbra serve`, and the `stack_provenance` agent tool (MCP / LangChain / LlamaIndex).

asset.description: Which product's raster was read, matching `to_stack(asset=...)`.

agrees.description: Whether `to_stack` would accept this selection's provenance. Only the provenance: a series can agree here and still fail to stack for an unrelated reason (footprints that do not overlap, a source that could not be read).

groups.description: The acquisitions grouped by what their sources say a pixel is, largest group first. When `agrees` is false, `groups[0].hrefs` is the subset to re-run on.

unreadable.description: Sources that could not be opened, reported apart rather than grouped: a failed read does not make the selection disagree, it makes the answer incomplete.

shared.description: What every readable source agrees on, exactly as `to_stack` carries it into `attrs["provenance"]`. Absent when they disagree, and also for the ordinary case of a series of untagged published products.

refusal.description: Verbatim the ValueError a stack of this selection would raise. Absent when `agrees` is true.

provenanceRecord.description: A raster's `UMBRA_*` conversion record, keys lowercased and de-prefixed. `"(unrecorded)"` is a raster with no umbra-py conversion provenance, such as a published GEC; `"none"` is a step that ran nothing.

record.description: Every measurement key, so a group of published GECs reads `"(unrecorded)"` throughout rather than as gaps.

count.description: How many acquisitions are in the group (the length of `item_ids`).

item_ids.description: The group's acquisitions, in the selection's own oldest-first order.

hrefs.description: The item JSON URL of each member, the arguments `umbra stack` takes. Shorter than `item_ids` when an item carried no URL (one built from a dict rather than fetched from the catalog).

href.description: The raster URL that could not be opened, or null when the item lists no such asset at all.
